//: Realtime Database rules for this app. Deploy with:  firebase deploy --only database
The app decides what a user may do by reading users/$uid/role in LoginActivity and
showing the admin screens when it says 'admin'. That check lives on the client, so
it is a convenience, not a control: anyone holding the app's config can talk to the
database directly and never run that code. These rules are where the actual limits
are, and they mirror the client's intent on the server side.
Note the shape of the users rule. There is deliberately no .write at the $uid level,
because a granted write cascades to every child below it — one blanket rule there
would let any signed-in user set their own role to 'admin'. Permissions are granted
field by field instead, and role can only be set to 'customer', once, at sign-up.
